Check if a value is the name of a valid log level.

## Signature

```typescript
static isLogLevel(value: unknown): value is LogLevel;
```

## Parameters

## Returns

value is [LogLevel](/logger-ts/docs/api/logger/typealiases/loglevel)

True if the value is a valid log level name.

## Remarks

It is a type guard, to be used when the level comes from a source that is not checked by the compiler, like a command line option or an environment variable. It returns `false` for any value that is not one of the strings in `levelNames`<!-- -->, including non-string values, strings with different case, and the names of inherited properties (like `'toString'`<!-- -->).

- added in v7.0.0

## Example


```javascript
const name = process.env.LOG_LEVEL
if (Logger.isLogLevel(name)) {
  log.level = name
} else {
  log.error(`Level must be one of: ${Logger.levelNames.join(', ')}`)
}
```
